transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mrs. Fitzgerald. Please, come in and sit down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you. I am just... it is very hard today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you are feeling very overwhelmed. I want to start by saying I have some news about your follow-up care that is not good.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it my heart? Is something wrong with the medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, your health is doing fine. But I made a mistake with your paperwork. I gave you a clinic for your next visit, but that clinic does not take your insurance.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My insurance? I do not understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means the clinic will not pay for your visit. They will ask you for a lot of money. I gave you the wrong place to go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh no. No, no. I cannot pay that. My husband, he handled everything. Since he passed... I have nothing. I have no money for this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am so sorry. I take full responsibility for this mistake. It was my job to check your insurance, and I did not do it correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel so alone in this. I try to do what the papers say, but it is so confusing. Arthur always knew what to do.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like you are feeling very lost without him to help you navigate this. It is a huge burden to carry by yourself.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is. It is a very big burden.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to sit here with you for a moment. We do not have to rush. I know this is a lot to take in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I was not careful enough when I wrote your instructions. I apologize for the stress this is causing you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So now what? I have no doctor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am going to fix this. To make sure I am being clear, can you tell me what you understand happened with the clinic?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You gave me a place that costs too much money.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. Now, I am going to find a new clinic for you. This new place will definitely take your insurance so you do not pay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will it be far? I cannot drive long.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will look for one close to your home. I will call them today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I cannot believe I have to deal with more papers.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it feels like too much right now. It is exhausting to have to fix a mistake that I made.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. It is very tiring.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am staying on this until it is solved. I will find a doctor and I will call your daughter to help you with the appointment. Is that okay?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, Sarah can help.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will find the name of the new doctor and the address. I will give you a new paper. When do you think you can check your phone for my call?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Maybe tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call you by noon tomorrow with the name of the new clinic. Then, I will send the paper to your house. Does that sound like a good plan?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose so.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will make sure this is handled. I do not want you to worry about this one more time.

H.justification: Resident allows full pauses, explicitly states 'we do not have to rush,' and never interrupts the patient.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and comprehension is checked once ('can you tell me what you understand happened').

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am so sorry', 'I apologize') and takes full personal responsibility without deflection.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('overwhelmed', 'lost', 'exhausting') and references the patient's loss of her husband.

T.justification: Resident provides specific next steps (find new clinic, call daughter) with a timeline (by noon tomorrow) and a patient role (checking phone), but does not address how to prevent the error in the future.
